title: Morton hires the Russell band and books the Wilkes-Barre date
summary: Russell's band takes two weeks off and Morton hires it for a tour, renting Cadillacs and promising a promoter a packed house.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: One time, we were at the Saratoga Club, and we were working the whole year round, not even one night off in the whole year. So we told Russell, we said, man, we're tired. We're going to leave there. We're going to the Roseland Ballroom two months back to Saratoga. Tour, make theater, Lowest State and all those places, go to Washington, D.C., come back. So finally we took two weeks off. Russell put another band in the Saratoga, and said, well, these fellas have two weeks. And Jelly was there that night. He heard about it. He said, Russell, I want to use your band. I said, it's okay, because next week we'll be off two weeks. And then he started sending these Steelers out, you know, for two of them. He said, Russell, I'm going to give you $50 a night to stay home. That's right. Now this is funny. I'm going to give you $50 a night to stay home. I don't need you. But your band. Took the whole band in tight. He didn't tell us how much he was going to pay us yet. But he told Russell, I remember that. Bob Foster, Red Island, Otis Johnson, Agen Bollett, we had one trombone at the time. Three Reeds, Greeley Walton, myself, and Charlie Holmes. And we had a solid match. Took our arrangements and took his arrangements. He had some good arrangements, too. So we rehearsed his arrangements in the daytime privately. We didn't let nobody know that he's taking our band. He's got, the first game we played was in Wilts Bay, Pennsylvania. Jelly went out and rented some Cadillacs. He rented about three times. He rented about three times. He rented about three times. He rented about three times. Second-hand, you know. And I drove one up myself. That's right. I drove one with about four to five guys in the band. And Red wasn't driving there. And we went in style. When we get to Wilts Bay, Pennsylvania, Jelly had played there before with a bad band. It didn't have no people in the place, you know. And the guy who was kind of salsa dear And the guy was kind of strong, he said, well, Jelly, Jelly said, man, I got a band tonight. The man said, oh, Jelly, don't give me that stuff, man. You brought me a band last year. Jelly said, but now, tonight, man, I'm going to pack your place. He had two gigs there, you know, two nights. He said, tomorrow night the police will have to keep the people in line.
The man said, oh, Jelly, come on, come on.

If I have 150 people, I'll make it. And the police hold about 500. This was in a big park. And they had no broadcasting. The cats would come in the head of you by the window, see what kind of band you got. And if it was a good band, they'd tell us, and they'd come in. If it was a bad band, nobody happened.
Jelly said, oh, man, tonight I'm back to the place.
So, tomorrow night you'll get a compliment.
